name: Vegan Blueberry Muffins with Coconut Milk
description: Deliciously moist and fluffy vegan blueberry muffins featuring a tender crumb thanks to coconut milk and vital wheat gluten. A perfect dairy-free and egg-free breakfast treat.

dry.name: Powdered egg replacer
dry.notes: Equivalent to 2 eggs, check package for specific instructions.

wet.name: Neutral oil
wet.notes: Such as canola or melted coconut oil.

wet.name: Water
wet.notes: For mixing with the egg replacer.

instructions: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or lightly grease it.
In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, vital wheat gluten, baking powder, powdered egg replacer, and salt until well combined.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the coconut milk, oil, water, and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet ingredients into the bowl with the dry ingredients. Stir with a spatula until just combined. Do not overmix; a few lumps are okay.
Gently fold in the blueberries. If using frozen blueberries, toss them with a tablespoon of flour from the dry ingredients before folding in to prevent sinking.
Divide the batter evenly among the 12 prepared muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the tops are golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.
Let the muffins cool in the tin for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: For a crunchy topping, sprinkle a little coarse sugar on top of the muffins before baking. If you don't have vital wheat gluten, you can omit it, but the texture will be slightly more crumbly.
